The saved copy of the city draft permit (https://web.archive.org/web/20260516170502/https://louisvilleky.gov/sites/default/files/2026-05/C-0127-22-0046-V%20(R2)_Draft.pdf) says 660 MW net output, which matches the net winter figure and not the nameplate.

Fuel.note: The Louisville draft air permit for Mill Creek unit 5 is gone from the city site, so I read the saved copy from May 2026 (https://web.archive.org/web/20260516170502/https://louisvilleky.gov/sites/default/files/2026-05/C-0127-22-0046-V%20(R2)_Draft.pdf). It describes a natural gas fired combined cycle unit and lists a diesel emergency generator of 2000 kilowatts and a diesel fire pump on the same permit. The diesel is burned in those small engines, not in the turbine, so the permit only partly supports the diesel entry. The EIA-860M table for September 2026 lists natural gas only for generator 5.

Status.note: The LG&E and KU fourth 60-day project update for Mill Creek Unit 6, filed September 30, 2026 (https://psc.ky.gov/pscecf/2025-00313/andrea.fackler%40lge-ku.com/09302026113016/02-LGE-KU_MC6_Project_Update_Rpt_4.pdf), says the engineering contract is still out to bid and the companies expect to sign it by the end of the first quarter of 2027. Only $43.7 million has been spent so far. The June 2026 development timeline (https://psc.ky.gov/pscecf/2025-00313/rick.lovekamp%40lge-ku.com/06052026025205/03-2025-00313_JI_DR1_LGE_KU_Attach_to_Q5%28c%29_-_MC6_Development_Timeline.pdf) shows construction starting after the contract is signed. So the unit is not under construction. The Energy and Information Project listing of under construction is not supported. This also gives a live source for the pre-construction status.

qa.question: Should Backup Power stay no for Mill Creek unit 6?
qa.finding: The saved copy of the Louisville draft air permit lists one 2,180 kilowatt diesel emergency generator and one diesel fire pump for unit 6. The main unit is a combined cycle block and not a backup engine fleet.
qa.recommendation: Leave Backup Power as no for the unit. The small emergency generator is too small to add as its own unit.
qa.note: I read the saved copy of the permit at https://web.archive.org/web/2026/https://louisvilleky.gov/sites/default/files/2026-05/C-0127-25-0007-V_Draft.pdf. It lists only emergency equipment for the plant itself. The permit for unit 5 at https://web.archive.org/web/20260516170502/https://louisvilleky.gov/sites/default/files/2026-05/C-0127-22-0046-V%20(R2)_Draft.pdf lists a 2000 kilowatt emergency generator and a fire pump in the same way. Neither permit names a data center or a backup fleet.

qa.question: Is 740 MW or 660 MW the right nameplate for Mill Creek unit 5?
qa.finding: The EIA table for September 2026 gives 740 MW nameplate and 660 MW net winter. The draft city permit said 660 MW and the certificate application said 680 MW.
qa.recommendation: Keep 740 MW, which is the nameplate. Do not use the lower permit figure.
qa.note: Source: https://www.eia.gov/electricity/data/eia860m/xls/september_generator2026.xlsx. I could not open the dead city permit page to read the permit wording.

qa.question: Do the coal unit 2 retirement notes need a human update?
qa.finding: The Status Detail text says coal unit 2 may run until at least 2031. EIA still lists unit 2 as operating with no planned retirement year. I made no change to the coal rows.
qa.recommendation: Leave the coal rows to the coal reviewer and add a note in the plant summary that unit 2 may run until at least 2031.
qa.note: The 2025-00313 filing from June 2026 titled for not retiring Mill Creek 2 is at https://psc.ky.gov/pscecf/2025-00313/rick.lovekamp%40lge-ku.com/06052026025205/09-2025-00313_JI_DR1_LGE_KU_Attach_to_Q8_-_Att_1_MC5_NGCC_Amendment_Not_Retire_MC2.pdf. It is a June 2026 filing in the same case.

qa.question: Should diesel stay in the fuel entry for Mill Creek units 5 and 6?
qa.finding: The EIA-860M table for September 2026 lists natural gas only for unit 5. The air permits show diesel only in emergency generators and fire pumps, not in the turbines.
qa.recommendation: Ask the project manager whether diesel belongs in the fuel entry. If the turbines have no diesel backup, change the fuel to natural gas only.
qa.note: Sources: https://web.archive.org/web/20260516170502/https://louisvilleky.gov/sites/default/files/2026-05/C-0127-22-0046-V%20(R2)_Draft.pdf and https://web.archive.org/web/2026/https://louisvilleky.gov/sites/default/files/2026-05/C-0127-25-0007-V_Draft.pdf. I found no document that says the turbines can burn diesel.
